source.title: Learning Theory Can (Sometimes) Explain Generalisation in Graph Neural Networks
source.authors: P. Esser; L. C. Vankadara; Debarghya Ghoshdastidar

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes graph neural networks in transductive node classification and reports empirical generalization results for synthetic SBM and Cora settings, extending generalization analysis to a different modality and task than the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports empirical results on graph-feature alignment, graph size, number of labeled nodes, depth, and residual connections. Its learning-theoretic bounds and discussion of prior work are not empirical result rows. It does not test the listed claim versions' specific setups.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes transductive GNN generalization bounds and empirical trends on SBM and Cora. None of its results tests V1–V8. A new task alone does not qualify as T3 without a result bearing on a listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Under suitable distributional assumptions, transductive Rademacher-complexity bounds explain some GNN generalization trends. Residual connections improve the tested empirical outcomes, while the predicted exponential dependence on depth is only partly reflected empirically. The experiments validate trends rather than the numerical tightness of the bounds.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies graph convolutional networks for transductive node classification under synthetic SBM and Cora settings; it does not use the listed versions' image or language setups. Its experiments use SGD for SBM and Adam for Cora; residual experiments use connections to the first layer, which the appendix says deviates from the formal model.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured outcomes vary with feature-graph alignment, graph size, number of labeled nodes, depth, and residual connection α.

fits_no_version.finding: SBM generalization error increases with graph-feature alignment. Cora feature-noise experiments show a similar reported trend, but do not directly measure alignment. Error remains mostly consistent across tested graph sizes and declines initially as the labeled fraction increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transductive GNN generalization loss depends on feature structure and label availability, while remaining approximately stable across the graph sizes tested here.

fits_no_version.finding: For SBM and Cora, error increases most clearly through the first three layers and then grows more slowly. Residual models have lower reported error than vanilla GNNs, with ordering across residual weights consistent with the theoretical prediction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth and residual connections affect transductive GNN generalization loss, with first-layer residual connections improving the tested models.

record.problems: The empirical figures do not provide numerical values in the text. The paper states that absolute bound values are outside the plotted (0, 1) range, so it plots trends only. Experiments average over five random initializations for the SBM settings; no error bars are stated. The authors note that the empirical depth trend deviates from the theoretical bound. Residual experiments use a connection to the first layer rather than the formal feature-level connection.
record.rows_left_out: No reported empirical result meeting the row criteria was omitted. Theoretical bound derivations, cited prior results, and figure values not described in the text were not entered as empirical rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and matched natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error and their test-error trends.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Matched adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparisons under specified tuning budgets. Using different optimizers on different datasets supplies no such comparison.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and ranking against competing measures.
Removing examples selected by memorization influence versus matched random removal and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; this does not dispute the reported GNN trends. The study's theoretical graph-versus-no-graph comparisons do not test V3's image-classifier claim. Appendix F.2 notes that trend visibility depends on learning rate, and theoretical curves are rescaled for plotting.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label memorization or matched natural-label versus random-label experiment.
No width sweep beyond interpolation or test-error peak analysis.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected image classifiers or local connectivity.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No batch-size sweep or fixed-epoch large-batch comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized examples or retraining comparison.

rows.subject: GNN
rows.size_stated: one layer; hidden layer size d1 = 16
rows.operation_detail: Measured generalization error while varying latent alignment between node features and graph structure.
rows.value: The generalisation error increases with an increase in the latent structure.
rows.uncertainty: Mean over 5 random initialisation; no error bar stated.
rows.note: The paper reports the direction of the trend, not point values.
rows.check: The alignment trend is reported, but it measures none of V1–V8. The outcome uses squared loss rather than classification error.

rows.subject: GNN
rows.operation_detail: Added Gaussian noise to Cora feature vectors and measured generalization error.
rows.value: The paper reports behaviour similar to the SBM alignment experiment; its preceding description says error increases as latent structure increases.
rows.note: The paper describes the trend as similar but does not give numeric values in the text.
rows.check: Feature noise is an alignment proxy; the authors explicitly cannot verify Cora alignment directly. Do not describe this as measured increasing alignment. The outcome uses negative log likelihood. Appendix F.2.2 inherits the one-layer, width-16 setup.

rows.operation_detail: Measured generalization error while increasing network depth.
rows.value: With increasing depth the generalisation error increases for the first three layers significantly, then the rate of growth decreases.
rows.note: The paper says empirical behaviour deviates from the theoretical exponential bound at greater depth.
rows.check: This varies depth, whereas V2 concerns width beyond interpolation. Partial agreement with the paper's depth bound is not a partial effect for any listed version.
